instruments.title: Zero-point ladder — one rung of R_N = ℓ_P φ^N
instruments.status: MODEL (declared: round S³, conformally coupled massless real scalar, one renormalization scheme, structural ansatz R_N = l_P phi^N) + VERIFIED arithmetic

inputs.name: N
inputs.doc: the rung index of the structural ladder R_N = l_P phi^N; N = 207 is the internal reference index near one light-second and is NOT recombination

inputs.name: beta
inputs.doc: the S³ scalar mode index; eigenvalues are lambda_beta = (beta^2-1)/R^2 with degeneracy beta^2

inputs.name: M
inputs.doc: the bare-sum cutoff. The bare sum DIVERGES; M is a cutoff whose value is displayed rather than hidden, and the renormalized Casimir term is the one that does not depend on it

inputs.name: theta
inputs.doc: reduced temperature k_B T R_N/(hbar c). Below theta = 1/ln 3 the thermal term is exponentially suppressed and the ladder is genuinely a zero-point ladder rather than a thermal one in disguise

verifiers: docs/verify-zero-point-csv.cjs (every column reproduced from first principles)

instruments.title: EBK quantisation — the semiclassical prediction against the exact spectrum
instruments.status: DERIVED (action integral) + VERIFIED against exact diagonalisation, including the 1/j^2 convergence rate; the licence to use EBK here was MEASURED in work package C2, not assumed

inputs.name: j
inputs.doc: the spin block. The EBK error falls as 1/j^2, so this is the knob that controls how good the semiclassical answer is — and the block is (2j+1)-dimensional, so it is also what it costs

inputs.name: beta_plus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_+. At zero anisotropy the top is spherical, every level is degenerate and there is no torus structure to quantise

inputs.name: beta_minus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_-

inputs.name: levels
inputs.doc: how many EBK tori to compute, each compared against its own exact doublet

inputs.name: quadrature
inputs.doc: samples in the action integral. The quadrature error is separate from the semiclassical error and must be pushed below it before any convergence rate can be read

verifiers: docs/verify-bianchi-ix-c2.cjs (13/13) — the regularity that licenses the method

instruments.title: Particle creation — what an anisotropic universe makes, and what expansion does not
instruments.status: DERIVED (exact factorisation + exact Bogoliubov system) + VERIFIED; conformal coupling and zero mass are ASSUMPTIONS, not results

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.doc: the starting scale factor. An isotropic point is on the constraint surface only above the bounce radius exp(2 alpha) = 3/(4 Lambda); below it there is no real p_alpha at beta = 0 and the seed is refused rather than moved

inputs.name: beta_plus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_+; zero with beta_- gives exactly zero created particles

inputs.name: beta_minus
inputs.doc: anisotropy coordinate beta_-

inputs.name: p_plus
inputs.doc: momentum conjugate to beta_+

inputs.name: p_minus
inputs.doc: momentum conjugate to beta_-

inputs.name: Lambda
inputs.doc: the cosmological term

inputs.name: j
inputs.doc: which spin block the mode lives in

inputs.name: level
inputs.doc: which level within the block, counted from the lowest. The adiabatic labelling of a level fails at a level crossing, and a crossing is not detected here

inputs.name: tauMax
inputs.doc: integration window in volume time

instruments.title: Spectral operator — H(t) = ½ Σ a_i⁻² K_i² on an anisotropic S³
instruments.status: DERIVED (operator and matrix elements) + EXACT (Jacobi diagonalisation, machine precision) + VERIFIED; the adiabatic interpretation is explicitly NOT claimed

inputs.name: alpha

inputs.name: beta_plus

inputs.name: beta_minus
